propositions: A failed git push on the async path (REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=async) discards all stderr output because the child process is spawned detached with stderr redirected to /dev/null and is never awaited, making the rejection warning undeliverable.

Library embedders calling rebar.comment() receive no push failure signal because the rebar root logger has only a NullHandler and install_stderr_handler runs only from CLI and MCP server, leaving writes silently stranded.

MCP write tools (comment_ticket, etc.) return only {"result": "ok"} to the agent because stderr is captured by the server, not delivered through the tool result, so rejection is invisible on that surface.

A durable marker recorded in the git directory (push_state.py) makes push rejection observable across all four paths by recording failure at the single _raise_if_strict choke point, independent of logging configuration or process boundaries.

The marker records terminal delivery failures (rejected, locked out, commit phase failures) but not non-attempt reasons (push-disabled, remote-not-found, invalid-destination) to avoid alarm fatigue from local-only stores that never attempt a push.

MCP write-tool results now include a push_status field {state, reason, detail, remote_ref, unpushed, since} via a shared WriteAckOut type, making rejection observable to agents without changing CLI exit codes or raising exceptions on the default path.
